session.question: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
session.answer:
The DECISION trial was a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase III study in patients with locally advanced or metastatic radioactive iodine (RAI)-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer. Treatment was continued until radiographically documented disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, noncompliance, or withdrawal of consent. After progression, patients could cross over to sorafenib depending on original assignment. (brose2011rationaleanddesign chunk 1)

Efficacy assessments were performed every 56 days (two cycles), and safety assessments were performed every 28 days (one cycle) for the first 8 months and every 56 days thereafter. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival, time to progression, disease control rate, response rate, duration of response, safety, and pharmacokinetics. (brose2011rationaleanddesign chunk 1)

The trial registration identifier was ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00984282. (brose2011rationaleanddesign chunk 1)

pqac-2a0e8ac5: The excerpt describes pharmacokinetic data from phase I through phase III roflumilast cream studies in psoriasis, including DERMIS-1 and DERMIS-2 phase III trials. It reports that roflumilast cream 0.3% was applied once daily for 8 weeks in the phase III studies, with systemic exposure assessed at Weeks 4 and 8. The paper lists ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers for the studies: NCT04279119, NCT03392168, NCT04211363, and NCT04211389. However, it does not mention the DECISION phase III study specifically, nor does it provide its design, endpoints, or registration identifier.

pqac-e45247c8: The excerpt is from a 2024 paper on long-term rilonacept for recurrent pericarditis in the RHAPSODY study. It notes that RHAPSODY was a phase 3 study of a once-weekly interleukin-1 alpha and beta cytokine trap (rilonacept) that reduced pericarditis recurrence, and that the long-term extension added 24 months of open-label treatment. The abstract states that continued treatment maintained response, while suspending treatment at the 18-month decision milestone was associated with recurrence. It also provides the trial registration identifier: NCT03737110. However, it does not include detailed DECISION phase III design, dosing schedule, or endpoints.
From Massimo Imazio, Allan L. Klein, Antonio Brucato, Antonio Abbate, Michael Arad, Paul Cremer, Antonella Insalaco, Martin M. LeWinter, Basil S. Lewis, David Lin, Sushil Allen Luis, Stephen J. pqac-47c94623: The excerpt describes a different trial: an open-label, randomized, active-controlled phase II study in 120 untreated advanced squamous lung cancer patients. Patients are assigned 1:1 to nab-paclitaxel plus carboplatin (135 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks; carboplatin AUC 5 day 1 every 3 weeks) or gemcitabine plus carboplatin (1,250 mg/m² days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks; carboplatin AUC 5 day 1 every 3 weeks). Primary endpoint is objective response rate; secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, and biomarkers. Treatment continues up to six cycles or until intolerable toxicity. Trial registration: NCT01236716.
From Jin-Ji Yang, Cheng Huang, Gong-Yan Chen, Yong Song, Ying Cheng, Hong-Hong Yan, Qing Zhou, and Yi-Long Wu. A randomized phase ii clinical trial of nab-paclitaxel and carboplatin compared with gemcitabine and carboplatin as first-line therapy in locally advanced or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of lung. pqac-b7068543: The excerpt describes a phase II risankizumab trial in hidradenitis suppurativa, not the DECISION phase III study. It reports that patients were randomized 1:1:1 to risankizumab 180 mg, risankizumab 360 mg, or placebo at weeks 0, 1, 2, 4, and 12. Placebo patients later received blinded risankizumab 360 mg at weeks 16, 17, and 18; all patients then got open-label risankizumab 360 mg every 8 weeks from weeks 20 to 60. The primary endpoint was HiSCR at week 16, with TEAEs as safety outcomes. Trial registration was NCT03926169.
From Alexa B. Kimball, Errol P. Prens, Thierry Passeron, Emanual Maverakis, Irina Turchin, Stefan Beeck, Leonidas Drogaris, Ziqian Geng, Tianyu Zhan, Izabella Messina, and Falk G. Bechara. contexts.context: This excerpt is about the CheckPRO phase II trial protocol in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, not the DECISION phase III study. It describes an open-label, randomised, two-stage trial with 80 evaluable patients receiving four cycles of ipilimumab and nivolumab with or without SBRT (24 Gy in 3 fractions) to one metastasis, followed by 10 cycles of nivolumab. Co-primary endpoints are objective response rate and PSA response rate; secondary endpoints include safety, radiographic PFS, clinical benefit, duration of response, PSA-PFS, quality of life, and overall survival. Trial registration is EudraCT 2018-003461-34 and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05655715.
